sources.entry: Agentic Workflow Patterns by ThibautMelen - A comprehensive and well-documented collection of agentic patterns from Anthropic docs, with colorful Mermaid diagrams and code examples for each pattern. Covers Subagent Orchestration, Progressive Skills, Parallel Tool Calling, Master-Clone Architecture, Wizard Workflows, and more. Also compatible with other providers.

summary.one_liner: A documentation-style collection that explains agentic AI workflow and autonomous-agent patterns (drawn from Anthropic's published guidance) with Mermaid diagrams and Claude Code component examples.
summary.what_it_does: The README is organized as a set of pattern pages covering foundations (augmented LLM, a 2025-2026 changes overview), six predefined workflows (baseline, prompt chaining, routing, parallelization, orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimizer), and autonomous agents (including a multi-window variant for long-running work). It maps Claude Code components (subagents, commands, skills, hooks) to their file locations such as .claude/agents, .claude/commands, .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md, and .claude/settings.json. It includes a decision flowchart for choosing a pattern and a rule that subagents cannot spawn other subagents, so all delegation goes through the main agent. The README also describes a "Patterns as Code" section with runnable pattern files that it says are checked in CI, and a repository structure with guides and use cases. The README does not include install or run commands for these files.
use_cases: choosing between workflow and autonomous agent designs
structuring Claude Code subagents, commands, skills and hooks
notable: Pattern selection flowchart that routes tasks to baseline, chain, orchestrator, autonomous agent or wizard
Maps Claude Code components (subagent, command, skill, hook) to their .claude file locations
Rule that subagents cannot spawn other subagents, with all delegation via the main agent
Patterns as Code section describing runnable pattern files
Heavy use of colored Mermaid diagrams for each pattern
caveats: The README describes itself as an independent community resource and not affiliated with Anthropic
No install or run instructions are given in the README for the runnable pattern files
Content is tied to Claude Code concepts; the claim of compatibility with other providers is not detailed in the README
